Q: Calling Fortran intrinsics in gdb A:

some intrinsics are defined in gdb (see for instance https://sourceware.org/gdb/current/onlinedocs/gdb.html/Fortran-Intrinsics.html), suppose x defined by x = [(i*i, i=1, 10)] then p size(x) returns 10. If you need more complex intrinsic like maxval you could use the pretty printer from mankoff (https://github.com/mankoff/gdb_fortran_tools) using numpy command directly in fortran like np max x

Q: Is there an efficient way to get the first non-zero element in an SIMD register using SIMD intrinsics? A:

  • PCMPEQB/W/D/Q against an all-zero register to get a vector with elements that are all-1 for the zero elements and all-zero for the zero elements.

  • PMOVMSKB to turn the vector of all-ones or all-zero into an integer bitmask. (Or movmskps or pd to get 1 bit per dword or qword, instead of per byte, if that makes your bit-scan -> index calculation more efficient, like if you want an element offset instead of a byte offset.)

  • invert that (C ~ operator, asm NOT instruction) to get 1s in the bitmap for elements that were non-zero

  • TZCNT or BSF that integer to find the first (lowest) set bit. Beware of BSF's behaviour if its input is all-zero. But fortunately that's not a problem when the input is an int ~bitmask - the high 16 zero bits become 1s. (An AVX2 version of this with vpmovmskb ymm that filled a whole uint32_t with possibly-1 bits could use ~(uint64_t)bitmask, or just use tzcnt since AVX2 CPUs also have BMI1.)

    In C++20, this is std::countr_one(mask) implemented as std::countr_zero(~mask). std::countr_zero has identical semantics to x86 tzcnt, including for input=0. If you're compiling without BMI1, check the asm to make sure the compiler optimized away any checks for input==0, since uint32_t ~mask is always non-zero for 16-bit vectors.

For example with intrinsics:

int first_nonzero_byte(__m128i v){
    //__m128i v = _mm_loadu_si128((const __m128i*)p);  // for a pointer arg
    __m128i vcmp = _mm_cmpeq_epi8(v, _mm_setzero_si128());
    unsigned bitmask = _mm_movemask_epi8(vcmp);
#ifdef __GNUC__
    return __builtin_ctz(~bitmask);
#else
    return _tzcnt_u32( ~bitmask );
#endif
   // returns 16 if v was all zero so ~bitmask is 0xFFFF0000
}

Compiles on https://godbolt.org/z/Y8vYbsW69 to

# GCC11.2 -O3 -msse4.1
        movdqa  xmm1, xmm0      # missed optimization, should zero XMM1 instead
        pxor    xmm0, xmm0
        pcmpeqb xmm0, xmm1
        pmovmskb        eax, xmm0
        not     eax
        rep bsf eax, eax        # tzcnt on new CPUs, BSF on old
        ret

In GNU C where _tzcnt_u32 won't compile without -march=haswell or something, we use __builtin_ctz. As I said, ~bitmask is guaranteed to be non-zero. tzcnt is encoded as rep bsf; old CPUs will execute it as bsf, producing the same result for non-zero inputs. New CPUs will execute it as tzcnt, which is more efficient on AMD (2 uops instead of 7). Intel executes either as single-uop. GCC uses rep bsf aka tzcnt if you don't tell it a specific CPU to tune for.

For a related function like shown in JATothrim's answer, using only 4 single-uop instructions (actually 2 uops for tzcnt on AMD) instead of 8 instructions including a pblendvb (2 uops on Intel). The shuffle/horizontal-reduction idea in that answer could possibly be useful if you want the element index as a shuffle control vector for vpermilps, but seems sub-optimal vs. this when you actually want a scalar int.

int equal_first_dword_bitscan(__m128i x, __m128i y)
{
    __m128i vcmp = _mm_cmpeq_epi32(x,y);
    unsigned bitmask = _mm_movemask_ps(_mm_castsi128_ps(vcmp));
    bitmask |= 1<<4;    // return 4 if the low 4 bits are all 0
#ifdef __GNUC__
    return __builtin_ctz(bitmask);
#else
    return  _tzcnt_u32( bitmask );  // runs as BSF on old CPUs, don't skip the OR
#endif
}

MSVC doesn't have __builtin_ctz, but will compile _tzcnt_u32 even if you haven't told it the target CPU supports BMI1. If you're definitely only running on CPUs with BMI1, you can leave out the bitmask |= 1<<4; so it will return 32 for not-found.

If you use trailing-zero count in multiple functions, best to wrap that ifdef stuff in a helper function, instead of at each use-case.

If there's only one possible non-zero value (like 1), PCMPEQB against a vector of that so you don't need to invert it later.

If that's the case, consider storing your data in a bitmap in the first place, to decrease your cache footprint by a factor of 8. Then you just TZCNT 64-bit chunks of the array.

Or for a larger array of data, search for the first non-zero vector with SIMD, then TZCNT the first non-zero element of it, if you expect there to be multiple qwords of zeros before the first set bit. Like memcmp does for finding the mismatching byte position.
See Efficiently find least significant set bit in a large array? and How to find the first nonzero in an array efficiently?

BTW, the asm instruction ref manual lists the relevant C intrinsics at the bottom of each entry, and you can search Intel's intrinsics finder by asm mnemonic. (See the x86 tag wiki for links).

Q: Get IP Addresses of 6 devices using MAC addresses using VB.NET A:

This is an old thread but I happened to have the same need so was looking for solutions.

The one shown is very slow and took 14 minutes to complete on my network. Also because the progress of async pings is not tracked, you have to guess and set the threading.thread.sleep to a real big number and hope it is long enough otherwise the process is still running when the code writes the incomplete data.

A better solution is to use a BackgroundWorker inside the Form, and have it write progress with each ping. I have written a solution which scans for ip, MAC, Name and uses a Lookup Data from a File to fill in gaps in Names not found, and whether device is wired or wireless. This solution takes 6 minutes on my network to run.

Below is a complete solution.

Create a Form named FormNet and add four controls to it.

ButtonRun, ButtonStop, RichTextBox1, BackgroundWorker1

Click on Run button to execute....

Imports System.ComponentModel
Imports System.Net
Imports System.Net.NetworkInformation
Imports System.Runtime.InteropServices

Public Class FormNET
    Public Const DevicenameI As Byte = 0
    Public Const ipnumI As Byte = 1
    Public Const MACaddressI As Byte = 2

    Public Const DevicenameLook As Byte = 0
    Public Const MACaddressLook As Byte = 1
    Public Const DeviceConnectLook As Byte = 2
    Public Const ipnumLook As Byte = 3

    Public LookupData(3, 50) As String, lookupTableEntries As Short, LookupArraySize As Short = 50
    Public NetWired(255) As String, NetiP(255) As String, NetMAC(255) As String, NetHostName(255) As String, NETDevices As Short
    Public BackgroundWorkerScanIsRunning As Boolean, CancelScan As Boolean, LookupDataAvailable As Boolean
    Private Sub FormNET_Load(sender As Object, e As EventArgs) Handles Me.Load

        Me.Opacity = 0.01

        Me.BackColor = Color.FromArgb(255, 32, 32, 32) 'very dark gray
        Me.Width = 1400
        Me.Height = 700
        Me.Top = 100
        Me.Left = CInt((Screen.PrimaryScreen.Bounds.Width - Me.Width) / 2)

        RichTextBox1.Left = 5
        RichTextBox1.Top = 5
        RichTextBox1.Width = 1380
        RichTextBox1.Height = 600
        RichTextBox1.ScrollBars = ScrollBars.Vertical

        ButtonRun.Left = 10
        ButtonRun.Top = Me.Height - ButtonRun.Height - 5
        ButtonRun.Text = "Run"
        ButtonStop.Left = ButtonRun.Left + ButtonRun.Width + 15
        ButtonStop.Top = ButtonRun.Top
        ButtonStop.Text = "Stop"

        Me.Opacity = 1

        LoadLookupData()
        'now click the run button to start scan

    End Sub
    Private Sub ButtonRun_MouseClick(sender As Object, e As MouseEventArgs) Handles ButtonRun.MouseClick

        CancelScan = False 'reset the stop flag
        CallBackgroundWorkerScan() 'start the scan

    End Sub

    Private Sub ButtonStop_MouseClick(sender As Object, e As MouseEventArgs) Handles ButtonStop.MouseClick

        CancelBackgroundWorkScan() 'interrupt the asyncronous scan process

    End Sub
    Sub LoadLookupData()

        Try
            'set Basepath to where you have your lookupDataTable.txt
            'format is Name,MAC,wireless or wired,ip if fixed else auto....see next two examples. each line ends in vbcrlf
            'Deco BE25 BR,10:5A:95:F9:49:B7,Wireless,auto
            'DENON Amp AVC-X3700H,00:06:78:4A:7B:9C,Wired,192.168.0.49

            If Not IO.File.Exists(basepath & "LookUpDataTable.txt") Then
                MsgBox("Error: Missing LookUpDataTable file so lookup data will not be used" & basepath & "LookUpDataTable.txt")
                LookupDataAvailable = False

            Else

                LookupDataAvailable = True
                Dim inputdata As String, x1 As Short, x2 As Short, x3 As Short, xcrlf As Short, n As Short

                inputdata = IO.File.ReadAllText(basepath & "LookUpDataTable.txt").Clone 'all the script file names, keyfile names, IP, MAC, Device names

                n = 1
                Do
                    x1 = InStr(inputdata, ",")
                    If x1 = 0 Then Exit Do 'end of string
                    x2 = InStr(Mid(inputdata, x1 + 1), ",") + x1
                    x3 = InStr(Mid(inputdata, x2 + 1), ",") + x2
                    xcrlf = InStr(inputdata, vbCrLf)
                    LookupData(DevicenameLook, n) = Trim(Mid(inputdata, 1, x1 - 1)) 'Data String between commas
                    LookupData(MACaddressLook, n) = Trim(Mid(inputdata, x1 + 1, x2 - x1 - 1))
                    LookupData(DeviceConnectLook, n) = Trim(Mid(inputdata, x2 + 1, x3 - x2 - 1))
                    LookupData(ipnumLook, n) = Trim(Mid(inputdata, x3 + 1, xcrlf - x3 - 1))
                    inputdata = Mid(inputdata, xcrlf + 2) 'get rid of this part of string and start at beginning of rest
                    n += 1
                    'grow the array dynamically if necessary
                    If n > LookupArraySize Then
                        ReDim Preserve LookupData(3, LookupArraySize + 20)
                        LookupArraySize += 20
                    End If
                Loop

                lookupTableEntries = n
            End If

        Catch
            'trap errors or core messages and display them in the message box
            MsgBox(Err.Number.ToString & " " & Err.Description & " " & "Error in LoadLookupData ", vbOK)
        End Try

    End Sub

    Sub CallBackgroundWorkerScan()

        If BackgroundWorkerScanIsRunning = True Then
            Exit Sub
        Else
            BackgroundWorker1.WorkerSupportsCancellation = True
            BackgroundWorker1.WorkerReportsProgress = True

            'start the asynchronous Task.
            BackgroundWorker1.RunWorkerAsync()

        End If
    End Sub

            Sub CancelBackgroundWorkScan()

        CancelScan = True 'this will get captured in the execution loop and force exit of tghe loop
        BackgroundWorker1.CancelAsync() 'cancel anyway as a precaution

        RichTextBox1.SelectionColor = Color.Green
        RichTextBox1.AppendText("SCAN Cancelled By USER....." & vbCrLf)   'show the message in the richtextbox
        RichTextBox1.ScrollToCaret()
        RichTextBox1.Refresh()

    End Sub
    Private Sub BackgroundWorker1_DoWork(sender As Object, e As DoWorkEventArgs) Handles BackgroundWorker1.DoWork
        Dim subnetBase As String = "192.168.0.", n As Short
        NETDevices = 0

        For i As Integer = 1 To 254
            Dim ipAddressString As String = subnetBase & i

            Dim ip As IPAddress = IPAddress.Parse(ipAddressString)
            Dim pingSender As New Ping()

            ' Use a short timeout (e.g., 500ms) for local network scanning 
            Dim reply As PingReply = pingSender.Send(ip, 300)

            ' If the host responds, query its MAC address 

            If reply.Status = IPStatus.Success Then

                NetiP(NETDevices + 1) = ip.ToString
                NETDevices += 1

                Dim macAddress As String '= GetMacAddress(ip)
                Dim destIpAsInt As Integer = BitConverter.ToInt32(ip.GetAddressBytes(), 0)
                Dim macBuffer As Byte() = New Byte(5) {}
                Dim macLen As Integer = macBuffer.Length

                ' Call the native Windows API 

                Dim result As Integer = ARP.SendARP(destIpAsInt, 0, macBuffer, macLen)
                ' If SendARP returns 0, the call was successful 

                If result = 0 Then
                    Dim macString As String = BitConverter.ToString(macBuffer).Replace("-", ":")
                    macAddress = macString
                Else
                    macAddress = "none"
                End If

                NetMAC(NETDevices) = macAddress

                Try
                    ' Extract the device name
                    Dim hostEntry As IPHostEntry = Dns.GetHostEntry(ip)
                    Dim deviceName As String = hostEntry.HostName
                    NetHostName(NETDevices) = deviceName
                Catch ex As Exception
                    NetHostName(NETDevices) = "none"
                End Try

                 NetWired(NETDevices) = "Unknown" 'Default
                'use lookup table to find a wired/wireless and a name (if absent) against this MAC
                If LookupDataAvailable Then
                    For n = 1 To lookupTableEntries
                        If LookupData(MACaddressLook, n) = macAddress Then
                            If NetHostName(NETDevices) = "none" Then 'only substitute a name if it was not found in scan
                                NetHostName(NETDevices) = LookupData(DevicenameLook, n)
                            End If
                            NetWired(NETDevices) = LookupData(DeviceConnectLook, n)
                            Exit For
                        End If
                    Next

                End If

                'check if stop button has been pressed
                If CancelScan = True Then Exit For 'allows for STOP

                    BackgroundWorker1.ReportProgress(i / 254 * 100)

                End If
        Next

    End Sub

    Private Sub BackgroundWorker1_ProgressChanged(sender As Object, e As ProgressChangedEventArgs) Handles BackgroundWorker1.ProgressChanged

        'show the message in the richtextbox.SelectionColor = Color.Blue
        RichTextBox1.AppendText("Found Ip: " & NetiP(NETDevices) & " MAC:  " & NetMAC(NETDevices) & " Device: " & NetHostName(NETDevices) & " Connection: " & NetWired(NETDevices) & vbCrLf)
        RichTextBox1.ScrollToCaret()
        RichTextBox1.Refresh()

    End Sub

    Private Sub BackgroundWorker1_RunWorkerCompleted(sender As Object, e As RunWorkerCompletedEventArgs) Handles BackgroundWorker1.RunWorkerCompleted

        RichTextBox1.AppendText("Scan Completed..." & vbCrLf)
        RichTextBox1.Refresh()

    End Sub

End Class

Module ARP

    ' Import the Windows SendARP Function from iphlpapi.dll 

    <DllImport("iphlpapi.dll", ExactSpelling:=True)>
    Public Function SendARP(
        ByVal destIp As Integer,
        ByVal srcIp As Integer,
        ByVal pMacAddr As Byte(),
        ByRef phyAddrLen As Integer
         ) As Integer

    End Function

End Module
